Subject: Recap: Technical deep-dive (latency/throughput SLOs / deployment topology)

Hi Maria / Evan,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the deep discussion. Below is a concise recap so we have alignment on pain, goals, and next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain points (as described by Acme):
- Intermittent latency spikes on current hosted LLM endpoint: P95 spikes > 300ms on 128-token responses during peak batch windows.
- Throughput constraints: need sustained 400–600 qps for inference front-door during peak (30 min windows).
- Cost sensitivity: must keep cost per 1k requests below your current budget target (you shared a target range; we will model).
- Strict data residency and audit requirements for some workflows (US-only).

Goals / SLOs you asked us to target for the PoC:
- Latency: P50 < 60ms, P95 < 200ms for typical 128-token generation workloads (90% of requests).
- Throughput: sustain 500 qps with headroom for 650 qps burst.
- Availability: 99.9% for inference endpoints during business hours, with automatic fallback to smaller model variant if capacity constrained.

Model / workload constraints discussed:
- Primary model family: candidate open LLM (instruction-tuned) ~7B parameters; evaluated quantized to 4-bit.
- Typical prompt length: 80–150 tokens; responses average 120 tokens.
- Prefer keeping KV cache warm for long conversation sessions (session lifetimes up to 20 min).

Proposed deployment topology (high level):
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) in US region with 3 availability zones for failover.
- Serving runtime configured for continuous batching + prefix caching; two model variants: primary quantized 7B (fast path) + backup 13B float variant for quality-sensitive calls.
- Smart routing: latency-first routing for web-facing endpoints; cost-favored routing for async batch jobs.

Attachments shared:
- redwood-technical-deep-dive-presentation.pdf (slides from today's call)
- acme-slo-requirements.xlsx (your SLO summary we filled during the call)

Open action items (owners):
- (Markus) Prepare initial performance/price estimate for dedicated pool (by Fri, 3/6).
- (Dev) Run internal benchmark using a representative 128-token profile and share results (ETA 3/9).
- (Marissa) Draft PoC plan and logistics including data access, test endpoints, and timeline (sent below).

PoC timeline (initial proposal):
- Week 0 (alignment): finalize SLOs & define test harness (this week).
- Week 1: provision dedicated pilot capacity and baseline benchmark.
- Week 2: run workload tests (throughput/latency) and iterate on batching/quantization tune.
- Week 3: finalize results and hand-off to your engineering for integration testing.

Next steps: please confirm the SLO targets above, and we will lock the PoC timeline. If okay, I'll send a calendar invite for a 45-min kickoff and share the Drive folder with the benchmark harness.

Thanks — talk soon,
\--
